s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption following sun exposure
salient_findings: Erythema and helical thickening with small blisters on ears
Vesicles on vermillion border and erythematous papules on cheeks, neck, and arms
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient had episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks prior
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Laboratory tests showed detectable PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
Virologic analyses negative for multiple viruses
Bacterial cultures from blister fluid were unremarkable

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption following sun exposure
salient_findings: Erythema and helical thickening with small blisters on ears
Vesicles on vermillion border and erythematous papules on cheeks, neck, and arms
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient had episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks prior
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Laboratory tests showed detectable PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
Virologic analyses negative for multiple viruses
Bacterial cultures from blister fluid were unremarkable

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of intensely pruritic skin eruption with erythema, helical thickening, and numerous small blisters, especially after sun exposure, along with the detection of PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA in lesional skin, is most consistent with erythema multiforme, which is often triggered by viral infections and can be precipitated by sun exposure.

rejected.label: eruption
rejected.why: Too general and does not specify a particular condition

rejected.label: eczema
rejected.why: Typically presents with more chronic symptoms and does not usually include small blisters

rejected.label: dermatitis
rejected.why: A broader term that encompasses many types of skin inflammation, not specifically matching the patient's acute presentation

rejected.label: urticaria
rejected.why: Characterized by wheals, which are not described in the patient's presentation
